findings.title: Disclosure scopes filing-text quotes to guidance only, but the note now also cites balance-sheet and liquidity quotes
findings.detail: The last Disclosures bullet says figures are generated by code from SEC XBRL data '(and, for guidance, from verbatim filing quotes)'. The round-2 note also cites non-guidance filing-text figures through [[Q-11]] (marketable debt securities 34,143), [[Q-12]] (marketable equity securities 42,783) and [[Q-13]] ($56.6bn / $42.8bn liquidity), all from periodic.txt, and it reports analyst offline results (target sensitivity, 'about two percentage points', WACC thresholds). Those offline results are labelled Judgment and 'analyst's offline check' in the body, so nothing is mislabelled there. The parenthetical in the disclosure is just narrower than what the note actually uses. The quotes are verbatim (they pass the gate) and the figures are correct, so this is minor.

findings.title: Net cash still omits $34.1B marketable debt securities (and $42.8B marketable equity securities); published target price unchanged by the fix
findings.detail: Round 2 numerical/recompute/valuation.json (identical to computed/) still has net_cash = cash 22.443B + short_term_investments 0 - debt 33.366B = -10.923B. The 2026-07-26 balance sheet reports marketable debt securities of 34,143m (Q-11; Treasury 33,003m Q-15 plus agency 1,140m Q-16; the company reports cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities of 56,586m, Q-14) and marketable equity securities of 42,783m (Q-12). Debt is complete. The generator has done what it can: gen-mapping re-verified that no snapshot concept or sum of concepts carries these balances; valuation_inputs.json rationales.net_cash gives a reasoned treatment (debt securities at full value; equity securities at a 30% haircut, justified by $36.9B of lock-ups (Q-17), concentration and tax on unrealised gains; non-marketable securities excluded) and a preferred net cash of +53.168B; and the note quotes the amounts and says the rating does not change. I reproduced the offline figures with src/aicfinal/valuation.py dcf() and the blending formula at WACC 10.7%: code as published gives blended $181.53, TP $182, upside -13.2%; debt securities only gives $182.94, TP $183, -12.7%; debt plus haircut equity gives $184.17, TP $184, -12.2%; both at full value gives $184.70, TP $185, -11.8%. All are Underperform. Neither alternative in the required evidence has been met, though. valuation.json net_cash does not include the debt securities, so the published TP of $182 is still below the candidate's own preferred $184. No controller-recorded decision accepting the understatement exists: state.json, decision_note.md and the round-1 decision.json contain none. The note gives the effect only qualitatively ('raises the target only slightly'; 'margin to the Neutral band edge narrows to about two percentage points at most'), with no target-price figures. This is a code/controller issue, not a generator error (see the gen-lead manifest integration.unresolved). It stays major until either a code mechanism feeds filing-text balance-sheet items into net_cash or the controller records acceptance.
evidence: src/aicfinal/valuation.py value(): net_cash = cash + sti - debt
findings.required_evidence: valuation.json net_cash includes the $34.143B marketable debt securities (and either includes the $42.783B marketable equity securities with a stated haircut or gives a documented reason for leaving them out), with target price and upside recomputed; or a controller-recorded decision that accepts the understatement, with the note quantifying the target-price effect (about $1-3 per share; upside -12.7% to -11.8%).

findings.title: Sensitivity magnitudes in the note are spelled out in words, not supplied by code, and 'about two percentage points at most' misstates the range
findings.detail: The 'Judgment (net cash)' and 'Judgment (discount rate)' paragraphs and the Risks section give quantitative results as words: 'margin to the Neutral band edge narrows to about two percentage points at most', 'a WACC roughly half a percentage point lower ... (about a third to a half of a percentage point ...)', 'a cut of roughly half a percentage point or less'. None of these come from values.json or a quote. They pass the untagged_number gate only because they are written as words. They are labelled Judgment and can be traced to gen-valuation's offline check in valuation_inputs.json rationales.wacc and rationales.net_cash (Neutral thresholds about 10.19/10.29/10.37/10.41% vs 10.7%, i.e. 51/41/33/29bp; band margins 2.7pp debt-only, 2.2pp debt plus haircut equity, 1.8pp both at full value). The WACC wording is consistent with that check. The net-cash wording is not quite right: the margin is 1.8-2.7pp depending on treatment, so 'about two percentage points at most' understates the debt-only case (2.7pp). The more natural reading, that two points is the narrowest case, would need 'at least' or 'as little as'. This is not a figure error, because the rating is unchanged in all cases and the direction is conservative. It is recorded so the practice of spelling out offline numbers in words is visible to the controller (policies.md section 4: numbers come from code or sourced inputs).
evidence: computed/note_rendered.md#Model and valuation (Judgment (net cash), Judgment (discount rate))
findings.required_evidence: Either the band margin is described accurately (e.g. 'narrows to roughly two to three percentage points, about two in the least favourable case'), or code exposes the sensitivity values as values.json keys the note can cite.

resolved.evidence: The Model and valuation 'Judgment (net cash)' paragraph now cites [[Q-13]] ($56.6bn cash, equivalents and marketable debt securities; $42.8bn marketable equity securities), [[Q-11]] (34,143) and [[Q-12]] (42,783), noting they come from the filing and are in millions with the current period first (matches the balance-sheet header 'Jul 26, 2026 | Jan 25, 2026', periodic.txt line 255). It states that upside stays below -10% in every case and that the margin to the Neutral edge narrows to about 2pp at most. I re-ran this independently with src/aicfinal/valuation.dcf and the code's blending formula at WACC 10.7%. Code net cash gives blended 181.53, TP 182, -13.2%. Adding debt securities gives 182.94, TP 183, -12.7%. Debt securities plus equity at a 30% haircut gives 184.17, TP 184, -12.2%. Both lines at full value give 184.70, TP 185, -11.8%, which is 1.8pp from the band edge. The claim holds.

The note now says the net cash figure 'deducts total debt (short-term plus long-term debt)'. That matches mapping total_debt = LongTermDebt 33,366m = short-term debt 1,000 + long-term debt 32,366 (periodic.txt lines 299, 303) and valuation.json debt = 33,366,000,000.

valuation_inputs.json now uses WACC 0.107, the unrounded CAPM figure. The rationale explains that the round-1 round-down had no basis and shows the arithmetic: 0.9934 x 10.75% + 0.0066 x 3.7% = 10.70%; equity of 24,100M x $209.66 = about $5.05T; debt weight about 0.66%. I checked all of these. I reproduced the stated Neutral thresholds with code's dcf() and blend: on code's net cash, blended $188.45 at 10.19% against the 188.5 needed for TP $189, so the threshold is about 10.18-10.19%; about 10.28-10.29% with debt securities; 10.37% with debt plus haircut equity; 10.41% with both at full value. The note's Model and valuation (discount rate) paragraph and its Risks section state that a WACC roughly a third to a half of a percentage point lower would move the rating to Neutral. That matches the 33-51bp gaps. Moving to 10.7% takes the rating further from Neutral, but it is the computed figure the round-1 finding pointed to, not a rating-driven choice. The terminal share is 71.1%, under 80%.

The note's Model and valuation section states that peer TTM windows end in May-June 2026 (AVGO and MRVL in May, AMD in June) against July 2026 for NVDA, which matches the peers.json ttm_end dates 2026-05-03, 2026-05-02 and 2026-06-27. rationales.peers explains that the 'CY2025Q4' calendar label comes from code (xbrl.calendar_label, TTM-window midpoint) and records that it was flagged to the controller; the gen-lead manifest lists it under integration.unresolved. That is the 'flagged to the controller' branch of the required evidence. Correcting the label itself is a code matter.

The Disclosures section now says the accession, exact cutoff time and price date are printed in the Data and Sources block of the published PDF, and that the note is distributed only through that publication. Verified: the only publication path is scripts/eu.py publish -> publish.render. It renders note_rendered.md and injects st['accession'] (ReportScope macro and Data block), st['cutoff_utc'] (DataDate macro, and 'SEC EDGAR filings accepted at or before ...') and 'last close ... on the cutoff date' (src/aicfinal/publish.py around lines 146-167). This meets the second option in required_evidence. Residual: the price date appears in the PDF only as 'on the cutoff date' plus the cutoff timestamp 2026-08-26T20:36:00Z, which identifies 2026-08-26 unambiguously.

The Disclosures section now reads 'the earnings release exhibits (EX-99.1, EX-99.2) to the company's same-day Form 8-K, which was accepted before the cutoff'. Checked against snapshot/manifest.json (release_ex99_1/2 come from accession 0001045810-26-000073) and snapshot/filings.json (that 8-K was accepted 2026-08-26T20:21:19Z, before the 10-Q at 20:36:00Z).

The fourth Key points bullet is now '**Valuation (code output):**' (last close, target, upside, band). The interpretation is a separate fifth '**Judgment:**' bullet. The facts, code outputs and judgment are labelled distinctly.
